text: Age: 70
Occupation: Business Owner/Councilmember
My name is Pat Wilson, and I am a candidate for City Council.

My family moved to Rolling Hills almost 30 years ago. My children were raised here, and two of them still reside here along with my three grandchildren. While my kids are grown up, I was very active in coaching them in AYSO Soccer, Rolling Hills Little League, and Palos Verdes Peninsula Girls Softball. I may have even coached some of your children! I can think of nothing more important for my family, and all the rest of Rolling Hills residents, than safety, security, and local control of our zoning authority.

That's why, as your City Councilmember, I have been actively involved in making our community the safest city in Southern California. I have been a member of the Traffic Commission for almost 20 years, working side by side with the Sheriff's Department to ensure safety in our community for motorists, pedestrians, and equestrians and managing speed limits through traffic enforcement.

Our residents also deserve security from fire danger and land movement. I have served as a member of the Palos Verdes Peninsula Regional Contract Law Committee and Palos Verdes Peninsula Public Safety Committee for many years now. These bodies strive to make the entire peninsula a safer place to live, work and recreate. Through these committees, the Automated License Reader and Peninsula- wide AI wildfire detection camera network were established.

Local control of our community development is critical. That is why I have strongly supported carefully planned residences compatible with their surroundings. It is essential that we maintain legal compliance with State law lest they attempt to usurp our local authority and impose their vision of housing on Rolling Hills.

My professional life involves running my business, Fast Lane Transportation, Inc., a trucking and container storage company which I started in 1979, creating jobs and supporting the logistics industry. I'm also a veteran having served in the United States Air Force.
Finally, you may have seen me around town playing drums with various musical groups.

All of these broad experiences help give my life balance and create the opportunities to share in our City Council deliberations. I feel that I have more to give and would be profoundly grateful if to earn your vote.
Respectfully,
Pat Wilson

text: Age: 78
Occupation: Incumbent
I have been fortunate to have lived in Rolling Hills since 1986 and honored to have served on City Council since 2015.

When I first ran for Council, based on observations gained over years as an active community volunteer and Planning Commissioner, two of my priorities included preserving the unique characteristics of our city (open spaces, privacy, equestrian, views, vegetation, etc.) and continuing our sound fiscal policies. I emphasized several areas of focus supporting those priorities, including Fire Safety Actions, Land Use/Development Policies, Disciplined Budgeting and Spending Guidelines, and Increased Resident Communication and Involvement.

Almost twelve years later, my commitment to those priorities and to the city remains unchanged. Although new issues come up, I think those original priorities remain strong pillars for effective governance of our city.

That focus also provides consistent perspective as we deal with new issues, including recent state laws restricting local government's ability to determine our own land use policies, unfunded government mandates, land movement, property insurance cancellations, and canyon vegetation growth that contributes to our very high fire risk. I continue to work to limit the impact of these and all other challenges to our community and the superior quality of life we enjoy.

Sometimes issues before the Council are complex and require us to render extremely difficult decisions that cannot satisfy everyone. But on every issue, in accordance with our understanding of the laws and our policies, the Council works together to act in the best interests of our entire community.

I work diligently to be an effective part of that process. I serve on committees to develop recommendations for Council's consideration on some of our most challenging issues, including Rubbish Collection, Vegetation Management and Disaster Preparedness.

Like my fellow Councilmembers, I strive to make the best possible decisions for the city and our residents. I have never missed a council meeting, am accessible and responsive to residents seeking information or wishing to share their opinions, and liaison to several community groups. On issues large or small I believe I have demonstrated that I try to consider all sides of a matter, deliberate openly and honestly and work collaboratively to get things done.
I hope I have earned your support and respectfully ask for your vote for reelection to the City Council.
I can be contacted at (310) 541-8641 or email Leahmirsch@verizon.net

text: I am running for City Council because I believe our community deserves thoughtful leadership, practical solutions, and a genuine commitment to preserving what makes our city special. I believe I can offer a fresh perspective on familiar issues and a grounded approach to new ones. I aim to bring enthusiasm and renewed energy to the council chambers as we navigate and prepare for the future.

As a residential developer in the construction industry, I understand the practical challenges associated with city planning, zoning, and building regulations. I also recognize the importance of property values and land potential alongside preservation of the rural beauty we all enjoy. Homeownership in our community is unique and often long-term; I believe people should have the freedom to love the place they call home.

I care deeply about public safety and look toward new initiatives currently being developed by City staff. I recognize the benefits of implementing new technology systems like the Safe Network and the value of the existing Block Captain program that helps keep residents feeling safe, prepared and connected in times of crisis.

I appreciate the Council's commitment to fiscal responsibility, and I'm keen on continuing this mindful decision-making moving forward. As our state policies continue to evolve, my goal is to thoughtfully pursue progress while embracing the values and traditions that have shaped our past.

As a third-generation resident, I feel incredibly fortunate to have grown up in a community with such unique character. My childhood was spent almost entirely outdoors, exploring the trails that wind through our pastoral landscape. I want future generations to grow up with those same opportunities and to create cherished memories of their own. If elected, I strive to ensure we all can continue to experience the treasured lifestyle that defines Rolling Hills.
